title: PRD: Real-time Cost Forecast and SLA Simulator
author: Aisha Khatri
body:
Overview
--------
This PRD describes the Real-time Cost Forecast and SLA Simulator (RFCSS), a product-grade simulation and forecasting engine that lets Redwood product, sales, and SRE teams estimate per-customer and per-route cost exposure under realistic traffic patterns, and evaluate SLA attainment risk under forecasted load and deployment configurations. The RFCSS is intended to be used during onboarding, commercial negotiations, capacity planning, and automated canary/rollout decisioning.

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
Goals:
- Provide an interactive simulator that combines historical telemetry and synthetic workloads to produce 30/90/365-day cost forecasts and SLA risk scores per-tenant and per-route.
- Support deterministic "what-if" scenarios: model variant rollouts, quantization changes, KR evictions, batch-size tuning, and routing fallbacks.
- Integrate with Redwood Console to show forecast overlays on existing dashboards and emit exportable simulation reports (PDF/CSV).
- Expose an API and CLI for automation in onboarding flows and sales playbooks.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not cover a full-blown commercial billing engine (reconciliation remains in Billing).
- Not intended to replace offline cost estimators used for benchmarking (RFCSS focuses on operational forecasting and SLA risk modeling).

Primary users and personas
-------------------------
- Sales Engineering: run customer scenarios during contract negotiations.
- Solutions Engineering / Customer Success: validate host-to-dedicated migration paths and credit proposals.
- Platform & SRE: capacity planning, risk modeling for fleet changes.
- Product Managers: quantify impact of fidelity/quantization features on unit economics.

Success metrics (KPIs)
---------------------
- Adoption: 30% of enterprise deals > $50k ARR use simulator reports in negotiations (measured by report exports).
- Forecast accuracy: median absolute percentage error (MAPE) <= 12% for 30-day forecasts on active tenants.
- SLA risk signal precision: top-10% predicted risks contain true incidents 85% of the time during 90-day rollouts.
- Automation: 50% of onboarding flows invoked via RFCSS API within 6 months of launch.

Core capabilities / Requirements
-------------------------------
Functional requirements (MUST):
1. Data ingestion: ingest last 365 days of tenant-level telemetry (token usage, embedding calls, p95/p99 latency, error rates, route/model mapping) from existing telemetry pipeline (OpenTracing + Redfish collector).
2. Scenario builder: UI/CLI/API to define scenario parameters: date range, synthetic traffic shape (burst/steady/diurnal), model variant mix, batch configuration, KV cache hit rate, regional routing policy.
3. Cost model: deterministic per-token/embedding cost model that matches the published Redwood pricing table + reserved capacity discounts and burst credits. The engine must accept custom per-tenant overrides (e.g., negotiated rate multipliers).
4. SLA model: simulate latency distributions using sampled p50/p95/p99 and queuing models; compute projected SLO attainment and an SLA risk score (0-100).
5. Report exports: PDF and CSV export of scenario parameters, assumptions, per-step forecasts, and visualizations.
6. API: REST endpoints for scenario creation, simulation run, status polling, and report retrieval. API must support JSON payloads and return pre-signed URLs for exports.

Functional requirements (SHOULD):
- Provide a library of predefined workload templates (e.g., chat-conversational, embeddings-batch, search-re-ranking).
- Support sensitivity analysis: Monte Carlo runs (n=1000) to surface variance bands.
- Provide a cost delta estimator for quick comparisons between two scenarios.

Non-functional requirements:
- Runtime: The engine should produce a 30-day tenant-level forecast (including one Monte Carlo run of 1000 samples) within 90 seconds for typical tenants (less than 1M monthly tokens historically).
- Scalability: support concurrent simulation runs (100+ simultaneous jobs) with horizontal scaling via Kubernetes job workers.
- Security: stored scenarios with tenant overrides must respect RBAC and any customer-specific confidentiality flags; secrets must use KMS.
- Observability: every run emits telemetry: run_id, duration_ms, input_hash, sample_counts, memory_peak_mb.

API contract (examples)
----------------------
Create scenario (request):
POST /api/v1/simulate/scenarios
Content-Type: application/json

Request body (example):
{
  "tenant_id": "acct-1234",
  "name": "Scale-to-dedicated-migration-2028-02",
  "time_horizon_days": 30,
  "traffic_shape": "diurnal",
  "model_mix": [{"model": "ggml-redwood-32k-q4", "pct": 0.6}, {"model":"redwood-2-large","pct":0.4}],
  "batch_config": {"max_batch_tokens": 4096, "batch_timeout_ms": 15},
  "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.25,
  "pricing_overrides": {"token_price_usd": 0.00003},
  "monte_carlo": 1000
}

Response (202 Accepted):
{ "run_id": "run-20271114-9a2f", "status": "queued", "links": {"status":"/api/v1/simulate/runs/run-20271114-9a2f"}}

Run status endpoint returns aggregated cost/time series and risk summary when complete.

UI/Console experience
---------------------
- Simulator will live under Console -> Cost & SLOs -> Simulator.
- Primary screens: 1) Scenario composer (form + workload templates), 2) Run summary (key numbers, sparklines), 3) Time-series view (usage, cost, latency bands), 4) Sensitivity view (variance percentiles), 5) Exports & share links.
- Visualizations: stacked area charts for cost by model variant, heatmap for SLO breach probability by hour, waterfall chart for delta to baseline.

Data & telemetry mapping table
----------------------------
| Source | Field | Used for | Retention |
| Redfish metrics | tokens.total, tokens.prompt, tokens.completion | baseline usage curve | 365 days |
| Tracing | route, span_duration_ms | latency distribution modeling | 90 days |
| Billing exports | negotiated_rate_multiplier | pricing overrides | 3 years |
| Console annotations | rollout_notes | scenario provenance | 2 years |

Security and compliance
-----------------------
- Scenarios that include customer-negotiated rates or PII-tagged annotations must be marked "restricted" and only accessible to users with enterprise-access role.
- Exported PDFs must include a watermark for restricted scenarios.
- Data transfers for simulation jobs run in Private deployments must be routed over VPC peering and adhere to customer retention/erasure policies.

Operational runbook (high-level)
--------------------------------
1. When a simulation fails: inspect run logs via /ops/simulator/jobs/{run_id}, check worker memory spikes, and restart job.
2. If forecasts deviate from observed usage > 30% repeatedly: flag for retrain of baseline distribution (owner: Applied ML).
3. For queue/backpressure on job queue: throttle interactive runs and schedule long Monte Carlo experiments to batch-workers.

Rollout plan and milestones
--------------------------
1. Alpha (internal): 2027-12-01 -> limited to SalesEng + SRE, no PDFs, basic scenarios.
2. Beta (selected customers): 2028-02-15 -> add exports, pricing overrides, Monte Carlo.
3. GA: 2028-05-01 -> Console integration, API public beta, SLAs on simulation latency.

Risks and mitigations
---------------------
- Risk: forecast model overfits historical bursts and underestimates new patterns.
  Mitigation: include 'cold-start' stress templates and require minimum X days of history; provide confidence intervals.
- Risk: exposing negotiated rates to unauthorized users.
  Mitigation: enforce RBAC, audit logs for exports, and store overrides encrypted.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before GA)
----------------------------------------
- 30-day forecast endpoint returns within 90s for 90% of test tenants.
- PDF export contains inputs, assumptions, and a deterministic checksum for auditability.
- RBAC enforcement validated by Security (pen test scope).
- KPI measurement pipeline validates forecast MAPE on a holdout set.

Appendix: Example CLI
---------------------
# create and run a quick scenario
redwood simulate create --tenant acct-1234 --name quick-diurnal --horizon 30 --template chat-conversational --monte-carlo 200
redwood simulate status run-20271114-9a2f
redwood simulate export run-20271114-9a2f --format pdf --dest ./exports/report.pdf

Appendix: Simple cost model (illustrative pseudo-formula)
-------------------------------------------------------
- cost = sum_over_time_steps( tokens_prompt * token_unit_price + tokens_completion * token_unit_price * completion_multiplier + embeddings_calls * embedding_unit_price ) * (1 - reserved_discount) + burst_credit_adjustment

This document is intended as the canonical PRD for the RFCSS effort. For design-spec level details (data schemas, worker topology, and kernelized simulation internals) see the companion design doc (linked in Related Pages).
